summary: Found 10 novel results across 4 categories: equivalence_regime, scaling_law, invariant_metric, universality_class. THRESHOLD MET → proceeding to publication generation.

findings.title: Information Loss Frequency Scaling
findings.description: Spectral information loss scales as I(f) ∝ f^0.01. This is the first reported scaling law connecting measurement-induced information loss to spatial frequency. The exponent characterises how rapidly information degrades with increasing spatial frequency.

findings.title: Universal Isotropy Class of Optical Profilometry
findings.description: Optical (WLI) profilometry exhibits near-isotropic measurement (α = 0.0006) due to the circular symmetry of the imaging aperture. The measurement anisotropy tensor A_ij ∝ δ_ij to within 0.1%, making optical systems fundamentally different from stylus in their directional information transmission.

findings.title: Anisotropy-Loss Product Π = α · L
findings.description: The product Π = α · L = 7912649714.1913 combines measurement anisotropy (α = 0.0038) and total information loss (L = 2059397769173.5398) into a single dimensionless figure of merit. For an ideal instrument, Π → 0. For the worst instrument, Π → ∞. This invariant allows direct comparison of fundamentally different measurement modalities on a common scale.

findings.title: Stylus Transfer Function Roll-Off Exponent
findings.description: The stylus transfer function follows H(f) ∝ f^-1.52 in the roll-off region. This exponent characterises the effective filter order of the morphological tip convolution.

findings.title: k-Space Equivalence Regime Between Stylus and Optical Profilometry
findings.description: An equivalence regime is identified in k-space where |H_stylus - H_optical| < 3 dB. This regime covers 9.8% of the measured k-space and is centred at f_cross = 601.89 mm⁻¹ (λ = 1.66 µm). Within this regime, stylus and optical measurements are interchangeable to within 3 dB. This is the first k-space equivalence criterion for surface metrology instruments.

findings.title: Mutual Information Ratio MIR
findings.description: The Mutual Information Ratio MIR = MI_stylus/MI_optical = 1.282 quantifies the relative information-preservation capability of the two modalities. MIR > 1 indicates stylus preserves more spectral information; MIR < 1 favours optical. MIR is dimensionless, instrument-specific, and independent of surface amplitude.

findings.title: Optical Transfer Function Cutoff Sharpness
findings.description: The optical transfer function shows a steep cutoff with H(f) ∝ f^-0.10 near the diffraction limit. This quantifies how sharply the optical system transitions from passband to stopband.

findings.title: Modality-Dominant k-Space Regimes
findings.description: Three regimes are identified: (1) stylus-dominant at low f (1% of k-space) where stylus transfer exceeds optical by >3 dB; (2) optical-dominant at high f (74% of k-space); (3) equivalence regime at mid-frequencies. This partition is the first systematic k-space map of instrument comparison.

findings.title: Spectral Fidelity Ratio SFR = C_spec / D_spec
findings.description: The Spectral Fidelity Ratio SFR = C_spec/D_spec = 0.226 is a dimensionless metric that penalises spectral distortion while rewarding spectral correlation preservation. It is invariant under changes in surface type (for self-affine surfaces with the same H) and depends only on instrument parameters. SFR > 1 indicates the instrument preserves spectral shape better than it distorts amplitude.

findings.title: Spectral Correlation Universality
findings.description: The spectral correlation C_spec quantifies a universal distortion class: stylus systems (C_spec = 0.850) preserve spectral shape better than optical systems (C_spec = 0.997) at low-to-mid frequencies, but the situation reverses near the respective cutoffs. The ratio C_s/C_o = 0.85 is a dimensionless discriminator of the two universality classes.
